ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, shareholders, and authorized signatories against (i) the Egyptian AML/CFT Unit consolidated sanctions and terrorism financing lists; (ii) the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (iii) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) and Non-SDN lists; (iv) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list; (v) the Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT blacklists; and (vi) the domestic Egyptian PEP registry and publicly designated political figures. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is mandatory for any customer or beneficial owner qualifying as a Politically Exposed Person (PEP), including identification of source of funds and source of wealth prior to incorporation; PEP status must be monitored continuously and for a minimum of 12 months after the PEP ceases to hold public office. Ongoing transaction monitoring is required for the low-risk standard profile of the consumer polling and market research SaaS platform.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) One-Stop Shop digital platform (Invest in Egypt Portal, www.investinegypt.gov.eg), operating in coordination with the Egyptian Companies Affairs Authority (CAA) and the Commercial Registry (Al-Sijill Al-Tijari) of the Ministry of Trade and Industry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The primary registered legal name of an Egyptian Limited Liability Company must be in Arabic script. A parallel Latin-script transliteration is permitted only after the Arabic name has been reserved and cleared, and the Latin version must not alter the phonetic or semantic identity of the Arabic name. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered company name, trademark, or protected trade name, and must comply with the naming guidance issued by GAFI and the CAA. Foreign-founders must submit both the Arabic name and the proposed Latin transliteration in the same reservation application. The transliteration must follow the normalized transcription standards adopted by the CAA for the avoidance of false similarity with existing registrations.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Government-run names and references to 'Arab Republic of Egypt', 'Egyptian Government', ministries, or public authorities, requiring ministerial approval
National flag, emblem, royal or sovereign insignia, or any symbol suggesting state affiliation
'Bank', 'Insurance', 'Takaful', 'Reinsurance' - requiring prior Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) or Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) license
'Securities', 'Capital Market', 'Portfolio Management', 'Asset Management' - requiring FRA licensing and authorization
'Oil', 'Gas', 'Petroleum', 'Mining', 'Refinery' - requiring approval of the Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources
'Military', 'Police', 'Army', 'National Defense', 'Intelligence' - requiring Ministry of Defense authorization
'University', 'Academy', 'Institute', 'National Research' - requiring Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research approval
'Media', 'Broadcasting', 'Press', 'News' - requiring clearance by the Supreme Council for Media Regulation
'Charity', 'NGO', 'Foundation', 'Humanitarian' - requiring Ministry of Social Solidarity licensing
Names implying a different legal form, such as 'SAE', 'Foundation', 'Trust', 'Partnership' where the entity is an LLC
Names indicating a foreign sovereign, foreign government, or international organization without treaty-based authorization
Offensive, obscene, or provocative words contrary to public order, public morality, or Islamic principles
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon final rejection of a proposed company name by the CAA/GAFI name-screening committee, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal within 15 business days of receipt of the electronic rejection notice. The appeal must be addressed to the CAA Name Committee and accompanied by (i) the rejection notification, (ii) a legal memorandum arguing non-confusion with the cited prior registrations, (iii) trademark search results from the Egyptian Trademark Office (Ministry of Trade and Industry), and (iv) up to five alternative Arabic names in ranked order. The Committee must issue a reasoned decision within 30 days of submission. If the administrative appeal is dismissed, the applicant may either resubmit new names through the GAFI portal or file an annulment action before the competent Economic Court (Cairo) within 60 days, invoking the Unified Companies Law No. 149 of 2019 and the grievance mechanisms of Investment Law No. 72 of 2017. An initial name reservation may be renewed once for an additional 30 days upon application to the CAA before expiry, subject to payment of the statutory renewal fee; a name rejected on the basis of a prohibited token requiring a ministerial license will not be reserved until the required license or conditional approval is produced.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A purely virtual office consisting of a mailing address or digital mailbox without any physical presence in Egypt is not permissible for an Egyptian LLC conducting consumer polling and cross-border market research. The company must maintain a physical registered office in Egypt, as required by the Unified Companies Law and the Commercial Registry regulations, where statutory records, tax cards, social insurance files, and data-protection documentation can be inspected. A co-working flexi-desk arrangement with a dedicated physical desk, a documented postal address, and management supervision is acceptable for this industry, provided the address is genuinely accessible and is not used for activities requiring a specialized license. Full remote operation without a leased or co-working physical address will trigger a substantive compliance warning and potential suspension by GAFI, the Commercial Registry, and the Egyptian Tax Authority.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-high, quantified at approximately 55-65% probability during the first fiscal year. GAFI, the Commercial Registry, the Social Insurance Authority, and the Egyptian Tax Authority conduct unannounced on-site inspections to verify the truthfulness of the registered-office clause in the Memorandum of Association, and the Economic Court has upheld cancellation of registration where the registered address was found to be fictitious.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended), Articles 21-72 (Limited Liability Company); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registration Department
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association (Esaam) with GAFI Incorporation Application Form
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital under Investment Law No. 72/2017; however, the issued capital must be fully subscribed and at least 25% of the subscribed capital must be deposited in a temporary Egyptian bank account in the company's name before final registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the share subscription list appended hereto, comprising 1,000 ordinary shares fully subscribed and paid to at least 25% of nominal value, is hereby ratified and the initial paid-up capital of EGP 250,000 is acknowledged; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the company's registered office shall be situated at [Office Address], Cairo Governorate, Egypt, and the lease agreement is ratified; RESOLVED FURTHER, that Mr./Ms. [Name] be and is hereby appointed General Manager and Mr./Ms. [Name] be and is hereby appointed Chief Financial Officer, each with full authority to open bank accounts, execute contracts, file necessary registrations, and carry on the company's market research business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Commercial Registry Pre-Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (OSS) – online portal or physical branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request with two proposed company names in Arabic (with English transliteration) and the activity code 7320. GAFI will check availability against the Commercial Registry and reserve the approved name.
required_dossiers: Copy of passport or national ID of each founder
Power of attorney (if using a formation agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, promptly submit two alternative names within 24 hours; no additional fee is charged for a second review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and Authentication of Memorandum and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Legal Department and Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles in Arabic, sign by all founders, and have signatures notarized before the competent Notary Office. The document must include share capital, distribution of shares, management structure, and registered office address.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles in Arabic
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary flags missing clauses, amend the document in accordance with Law 159/1981 art. 22-25 and re-submit; GAFI acceptance is normally obtained within 5 business days of resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Temporary Bank Deposit Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any Egyptian commercial bank or bank designated by GAFI
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate account in the company's name under formation and deposit at least 25% of the subscribed capital, obtaining a deposit certificate from the bank.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or promise of lease for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional KYC documents, supply the GAFI preliminary approval and a certified board resolution (if any); for missing corporate identification, request a temporary identification number from GAFI OSS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Final Incorporation Submission and Certificate Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete incorporation file to GAFI OSS, including the notarized Articles, bank certificate, and formation fees. GAFI will issue the Company Incorporation Certificate and register the company in the Commercial Registry.
required_dossiers: Form for appointment of directors and auditors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a query or request for clarification, the formation agent responds within the specified 10-day correction period; otherwise the file is suspended. Re-submit updated documents with a cover letter to the GAFI OSS manager.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), National Social Insurance Authority (NSIA), Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Incorporation Certificate, apply for an electronic tax ID card, VAT registration (if applicable), and social insurance registration for employees. Also register the company with the reinforced Commercial Registry and obtain company seals.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ETA delays the tax card, obtain a provisional tax certificate and begin VAT filing using a pending number; for social insurance, request an official acknowledgment receipt to avoid penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no industrial manufacturing permit is required for a consumer polling and digital market research platform.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None mandatory; voluntary registration with the National Data Management Center (NDMC) for personal data protection compliance under Law No. 151 of 2020.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – office-based and cloud-only activities; no polluting operations or natural resource usage.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for office operations; must comply with general waste disposal, public hygiene, and electrical safety requirements under Law No. 4 of 1994 and its amendments.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance from the Civil Defense Authority for the office premises (installed fire extinguishers, alarms, evacuation plan), structural load inspection, and general workplace health and safety clearance under Law No. 12 of 2003. A police clearance for the building is also required for the operating lease.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) (Misaha al-Dara'eb al-Misriya); unified portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; e-invoicing system: https://invoicing.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: EG_LLC must first be incorporated through the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), then register with the ETA within 30 days of commercial registration to obtain the Taxpayer Registration Number (TIN / VAT ID). Procedure: upload incorporation certificate and memorandum of association; appoint an Egyptian tax address or tax representative; submit passport or civil ID copies of shareholders and directors; declare the business line (ISIC 7320); obtain the ETA unified registration certificate. VAT registration is integrated with the TIN and becomes compulsory once annual taxable supplies reach the statutory threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime; LLCs are compulsorily taxed at entity level at the 22.5% headline CIT rate. Available elections include consolidated VAT registration for wholly-owned group companies, VAT refund or offset election against corporate tax balances, and tax stabilization agreements for GAFI-approved projects under Investment Law 72/2017. Hybrid mismatch elections are not recognized; treaty relief claims require prior ETA approval.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 - annual taxable supplies (goods or services)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory under Law 67/2016 as amended: all B2B and B2C invoices and receipts must be transmitted in near real-time to the ETA e-invoicing platform (https://invoicing.eta.gov.eg) using XML/JSON schemas, digitally signed with the taxpayer's ETA-issued certificate, and presented with a machine-readable QR code. Clearance is driven by the ETA Taxpayer Information API; phased rollout applies by taxpayer bracket. Non-compliant invoicing blocks fiscal clearance and attracts fines.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported goods and offshore services (including consumer-panel survey SaaS and cross-border market-research subscriptions) are zero-rated where the service is supplied to a non-resident, is not directly consumed or used in Egypt, and the consideration is settled in foreign currency. The exporter must hold an export contract, file the export invoice in the ETA e-invoicing system, and be able to demonstrate foreign end-use on audit.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CED / AFC declaration filed through the CargoX EDA platform)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate evidencing receipt of export proceeds in Egypt
0%-rated export VAT invoice approved in the ETA e-invoicing system
Signed offshore service agreement and certificate of foreign end-use
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA audits zero-rated claims against customs and remittance records. Insufficient documentation triggers reassessment at 14% VAT plus statutory monthly delay interest, monetary penalties up to the full tax evaded, and suspension of the taxpayer's export-invoice clearing rights. Forged export documents attract criminal tax-evasion sanctions and personal director liability.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), the lawful foreign-exchange and banking regulator operating under Law No. 194 of 2020, the Foreign Exchange Law No. 114 of 1939 (as amended), and the CBE Rulebook; the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU) concurrently supervises AML/CTF obligations for all authorized banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations (since 1997), guaranteeing full convertibility for current-account payments and transfers; the EGP operates under a liberalized market-determined exchange rate restored in March 2024 under the IMF Extended Fund Facility, eliminating prior FX allocation queues. Capital-account transactions, including foreign direct investment equity capital into an Egyptian LLC, are permissible for non-resident shareholders, subject to routing exclusively through a CBE-authorized bank with BPM6-aligned purpose declarations and post-entry CBE/bank verification of the underlying share-subscription resolution and source of funds. Profit remittance is characterized as current-account repatriation of investment income; the practical hurdles are documentary rather than statutory, requiring CBE-authorized bank certification, Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) tax-clearance certificates, audited financial statements, and a valid shareholders' dividend resolution. There are no quotas or conversion ceilings on repatriation, but all FX movements must be traceable in the bank's CBE reporting systems.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Revenue from service exports (including cross-border consumer polling, market research SaaS subscriptions, and platform data services) must be repatriated to Egypt through a CBE-authorized bank within 180 calendar days from the later of invoice issuance or service performance; goods exporters receive the same 180-day window measured from customs clearance/shipment. There is no mandatory conversion ratio: 0% of export proceeds must be surrendered, and the LLC may lawfully retain 100% of repatriated receipts in foreign-currency accounts (USD/EUR) at its Egyptian bank. The bank monitors overdue export receivables through CBE electronic export tracking and will suspend FX operations and require a written explanation for any unrepatriated balance beyond the statutory timeline.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow (pre-incorporation 'company under formation' deposit account) + dual-currency Operational Account (EGP current and USD/EUR foreign-currency account)
Capital Escrow deposit + Operational Account (EGP current and USD/EUR foreign-currency account)
Capital Escrow deposit + Operational Account (EGP current and USD/EUR foreign-currency account)
Capital Escrow deposit + Operational Account with integrated cross-border transaction banking suite

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary banking relationship; Medium as a complementary settlement channel. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Revolut, Mercury) hold no CBE banking or e-money license and cannot lawfully hold EGP client funds, disburse mass payouts to Egyptian beneficiaries, or act as the company's principal treasury hub. Wise may be used strictly as a cross-border collection/payout rail settling into the Egyptian corporate account via SWIFT transfers. PayPal Egypt, operating under a CBE-recognized digital-payments arrangement, can settle EGP receivables into the local bank account. All funds must ultimately rest in and flow through the CBE-authorized bank account; no foreign EMI may substitute for the Egyptian banking relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence at onboarding is the mandatory rule for all Egyptian licensed banks: at least one founding director or partner holding legal representation capacity, together with each authorized signatory named in the account-opening resolution (or a notarized attorney-in-fact with a certified power of attorney), must appear in person before the bank's compliance officer in Cairo. Original passports with valid Egyptian entry stamps or residency permits must be produced. Remote or purely digital account opening is not available at NBE, Banque Misr, or CIB; HSBC Egypt may allow a recorded video interview for a non-resident director only as an exception, provided the board resolution and UBO documents are apostilled and the director still presents through a local authorized representative at the bank branch. In all cases, a physical touchpoint in Egypt is unavoidable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident foreign director/beneficial owner with no Egyptian physical footprint, triggering heightened CBE beneficial-ownership (UBO) screening and cross-border PEP/sanctions checks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled passports of all UBOs; certified excerpts from home-country commercial registers; six months of shareholder bank statements substantiating source of funds for the capital injection; police-clearance or good-standing certificates from the UBO's residence country; a written corporate-charter narrative explaining board engagement; and a formal commitment that all UBOs will attend the physical KYC interview in Cairo at account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mass-payout/P2P aggregation typology: high-frequency, low-value outbound payments to consumer panelists via PayPal Mass Payout and Wise, read by transaction-monitoring engines as an electronic-money mule or funds-aggregation red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Campaign-level sub-ledger mapping every payout to a unique survey-completion record and panelist agreement; the LLC's documented AML/CTF program aligned with Egyptian AML Law No. 80 of 2002 as amended by Decree-Law No. 4 of 2022; executed client contracts with commercial invoices for each survey wave; monthly payout-to-service reconciliation reports to the relationship manager; and merchant verification certificates from PayPal and Wise confirming the LLC's business status.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected shell presence: reliance on a virtual office or co-working address with no substantive Egyptian operations, conflicting with the bank's mandatory premises-verification visit.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered commercial lease or licensed business-center sub-lease in New Cairo/Dokki; utility bill in the LLC's name; dated photographs of the physical office with visible signage; ETA tax card reflecting the identical registered address; and payroll records of at least one local administrative employee if hiring has commenced.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound equity wire from a jurisdiction on FATF 'dark grey' monitoring or with elevated correspondent-bank scrutiny, creating correspondent-banking friction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-to-bank reference from the remitting foreign institution; notarized shareholder subscription resolution; remittance purpose statement coded as direct-investment equity; historical bank statements of the shareholder; and a post-funding source-of-wealth letter executed before a notary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment-rail disapproval: the licensed bank rejects PayPal/Wise as unlicensed money transmitters under Egyptian law and refuses to allow wires to those EMIs.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written treasury policy declaring the CBE-authorized bank account as the exclusive settlement point and demoting PayPal/Wise to secondary collection/disbursement conduits; platform terms of use; panelist agreements; data-processing contracts evidencing genuine survey services; and, where aggregate monthly turnover exceeds EGP 2 million, a proactive information-sharing relationship with the EMLCU through the bank's MLRO.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders must remit equity in USD/EUR via SWIFT MT103 from their home bank to the LLC's pre-incorporation capital escrow account or newly opened capital account at the Egyptian bank. The inward remittance form must carry the BPM6-based purpose declaration for Direct Investment – Equity Capital (FDI) in an Egyptian entity, together with the general-assembly subscription resolution and source-of-funds evidence. The bank verifies the documents, credits the funds, and upon completion issues the capital-deposit certificate ('Shahadat Al-Eydaa') required by the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) and the Commercial Registry before incorporation is finalized. The capital may remain in foreign currency or be converted to EGP at the prevailing market rate; no capital disbursement is permitted before the certificate is issued, and any subsequent shareholding amendment requires a new deposit certificate and CBE re-verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational and trade outflows are cleared exclusively through the Egyptian bank using SWIFT MT103 for service payments (contractors, overseas panelist mass payouts, cloud hosting, software licenses) and commercial letters of credit (sight L/C, usance L/C) or documentary collections for physical imports and high-value procurement. Each outbound wire must carry the correct BPM6 service category code (e.g., Business and Management Consulting, Computer and Information Services), and be supported by the underlying contract, pro-forma or final invoice, and ETA withholding-tax certificates where treaty rates apply. For panelist disbursements, the LLC may fund its PayPal and Wise operational float accounts from the Egyptian account via MT103 wires, provided each funding wire is accompanied by a campaign-payout register reconciling beneficiary, amount, and survey-delivery evidence; the bank's FX desk will block any wire lacking a verifiable underlying transaction or where the LLC's prior export-repatriation record shows overdue balances.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward contracts (USD/EGP and EUR/EGP) from CBE-authorized banks, tenors up to 360 days, permitted only with genuine underlying current-account or trade exposure (contracted export revenue or import liabilities)
Onshore FX swaps between EGP and USD/EUR balances, used for liquidity smoothing between the LLC's foreign-currency and local-currency positions, documented under CBE master-agreement guidance
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EUR) to match the multinational mix of survey-client revenues and panelist payout liabilities
OTC vanilla currency options (USD/EUR) with a licensed bank to hedge cross-border receivables volatility, subject to bank counterparty approval and underlying exposure verification

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on EGP: expressly not permissible for onshore Egyptian corporates; the CBE authorizes deliverable instruments only, and any offshore NDF hedging must be avoided to prevent bank-account termination risk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate declaration with audited financial statements and auditor's report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), Investment Monitoring and Compliance Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ordinary general assembly must approve financial statements within 3 months of fiscal year-end (by 31 March for calendar-year entities); e-filing with GAFI due within 30 days of approval and no later than 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fines escalate under Companies Law No. 148/2019 and its Executive Regulations; continuous default beyond 6 months triggers an administrative warning, and failure to file for two successive fiscal years may result in suspension of the commercial registration and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Minutes of the ordinary general assembly approving the balance sheet and discharging the directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI (incorporated within the annual filing set); signed original retained in the statutory minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: General assembly convened within 3 months of fiscal year-end (by 31 March); signed minutes must accompany the annual corporate declaration to GAFI.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the assembly exposes directors to statutory fines of EGP 1,000-EGP 5,000; unlawful distributions render directors jointly and severally liable to the company and creditors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Register status confirmation and five-year renewal surveillance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Commercial registration is renewed every 5 years; the annual surveillance confirmation and renewal fee installment are due every January for calendar-year entities.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-renewed registration suspends the LLC's capacity to execute binding contracts; late renewal triggers a 10% penalty on the registration fee; after 30-day notice, continued default results in deletion from the Commercial Register and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) confirmation and register update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI Beneficial Ownership Data System and the company's on-site UBO register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation due by 31 March for calendar-year entities; any share transfer or UBO change must be recorded within 30 days of the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance attracts fines up to EGP 20,000 (approx. USD 650) under Companies Law No. 148/2019 and AML Law No. 80/2002; repeated non-filing may suspend shareholder voting rights and trigger an AML supervisory penalty.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No turnover-based exemption applies: every Egyptian LLC must appoint at least one certified auditor and file audited financial statements annually, irrespective of size or revenue. The Egyptian Tax Authority may separately require audited accounts for cross-border service revenue claims even when statutory sales are below the standard threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) aligned with IFRS as issued by the Egyptian Ministry of Finance and applied through the Egyptian Accounting Standards Board; banks and listed entities use full IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Shareholders must maintain and annually confirm the register of members and the UBO register on each 31 March; every transfer of membership quota or change of beneficial ownership must be recorded in the statutory registers and filed with GAFI within 30 days of the event. Unrecorded transfers remain ineffective against the company, and the company must freeze dividend payments to a transferee until the transfer is registered.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - USD 1,000 per annum for a Cairo-based registered office / corporate secretarial agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 800 - USD 3,500 per annum for the certified statutory audit of a small LLC with cross-border digital revenue

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% (standard rate for resident LLCs under Law No. 91 of 2005, as amended)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, newly established companies located in designated governorates or engaged in priority sectors may receive a 50% deduction on taxable profits for up to 7 years, subject to capital thresholds, job creation, and export performance. Free-zone companies are exempt from corporate tax on export-related income. A 0.2% solidarity contribution applies on eligible corporate profits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 19 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing portal at eta.gov.eg.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with mandatory quarterly advance tax payments during the year)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within four months after the end of the fiscal year; for a 31 December year-end, the deadline is 30 April of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenues from Egyptian operations; residents include worldwide income, non-residents include only Egyptian-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only gross revenue attributable to sales, services, or business activities carried out in Egypt. Exclude foreign-market panel data sales income unless it constitutes a permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible cost of services rendered and direct production costs, including incentive payments to survey panel members.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must allocate direct costs only to Egyptian activities; panel incentive payments must be supported by records of identifiable recipients and payment confirmations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indirect operating expenses: employee compensation, cloud hosting, marketing, professional fees, and software subscriptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Current-year deductions require Egyptian invoices or tax invoices where applicable; cross-border cloud and SaaS costs are subject to WHT on non-resident service income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory adjustments, including tax depreciation, exemptions, capital gains relief, and offset of prior-year tax losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign head-office overhead may not be deducted unless directly attributable to an Egyptian permanent establishment. Tax-loss carryforward is limited to 5 years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transactions and mandatory transfer-pricing disclosure schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all cross-border transactions with affiliates, including intra-group service fees and platform licensing payments, and attach the relevant TP Local File if thresholds are met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed taxable income and resulting corporate income tax liability (22.5%).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-residents, compute tax on Egyptian-source income only; do not include the 0.2% solidarity tax unless the company is registered with an Egyptian permanent establishment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing may attract an administrative penalty between EGP 10,000 and EGP 50,000, plus a monthly late-payment surcharge of 2% on outstanding tax due. Non-filers may receive an estimated assessment increased by up to 150% of the deemed tax, plus interest. Directors may be exposed to additional penalty assessments in case of gross omission.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% (standard Egyptian withholding tax on dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders under Law No. 91 of 2005, Article 58).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced rate under an applicable double-tax agreement, the non-resident shareholder must deliver an original or certified copy of the Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty country's competent authority and duly legalised/apostilled. The Egyptian paying company submits the TRC alongside the periodic Withholding Tax Return (Form 41) and a completed treaty-relief claim schedule to the ETA. Treaty relief is only granted upon written application before payment or within the statutory claim period; the ETA may request additional beneficial-ownership documentation for holdings through PayPal/Wise or intermediary platforms.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on payments of royalties, technical fees, and intellectual-property consideration to non-residents is 20%. Statutory WHT on debt interest paid to non-residents is 20%, except for interest on publicly issued instruments or bank deposits, which may attract a 10% rate. DTA protocols commonly reduce interest and royalty WHT rates to 10% or 15%, provided the recipient is the beneficial owner and satisfies substance conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 10,000,000 for the mandatory Local File and Master File; however, a simplified transfer-pricing disclosure schedule (Part of Form No. 19) is mandatory for any fiscal year in which aggregate related-party transactions exceed EGP 1,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not apply a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) code; nevertheless, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule under Article 142 of Law No. 91 of 2005, together with commercial substance jurisprudence, empowers the ETA to disregard artificial arrangements and shell companies. The ETA expects actual place of effective management in Egypt, documented board meetings, local payroll, physical records, and an operational commercial purpose. Where a market-research platform is booked in Egypt but managed entirely abroad without substance, the ETA can re-characterise the vehicle as transparent and assess taxes on the controlling foreign owners.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of income received via PayPal Mass Payout or Wise from the Corporate Tax Return, use of unregistered foreign accounts, or issuance of fabricated expense invoices to reduce taxable profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment up to five years and a fine between EGP 100,000 and EGP 1,000,000 under Article 133 of Law No. 91 of 2005; additional civil penalty of 100% of the evaded tax and judicial attachment of bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers, and de facto managers may be jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and penalties; travel bans and asset freezes can be issued at the request of the ETA under the Tax Collection Regulations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating or holding an Egyptian LLC with no physical office, personnel, board minutes, or operational records while attributing material profits to Egypt for treaty advantages or to defer foreign CFC taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA may disregard the shell, assess the controlling beneficiary personally at the full 22.5% corporate rate, and apply a 100% add-on penalty; persistent inactivity may lead to striking off from the Commercial Register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil upon a showing of fraud or sham; directors are personally liable for restitution of evaded taxes and may be prohibited from leaving Egypt until dues are settled.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Beneficial Ownership Disclosure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register the LLC or its parent with the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit, omission of beneficial-owner disclosure, or failure to report suspicious mass-payout transactions in sample-panel compensation flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines between EGP 500,000 and EGP 2,000,000 and imprisonment from two to seven years under Law No. 80 of 2002 as amended by Law No. 48 of 2022; possible cancellation of the commercial registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are personally liable for first-instance AML violations; conviction results in disqualification from board positions, travel restrictions, and freezing of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or file the Local File / Master File after surpassing the EGP 10,000,000 threshold, or incorrect/non-filed TP disclosure in the annual return for controlled transactions exceeding EGP 1,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Monetary penalties of EGP 1,000 to EGP 50,000 per infraction, coupled with the ETA's authority to re-determine taxable profits using OECD-compliant transfer-pricing methods and to levy an additional 50% assessment penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers who knowingly approved incomplete TP documentation can be personally assessed for the resulting deficiency and penalties; the ETA may further issue criminal referral for taxpayer fraud if false documents were filed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful Profit Repatriation and Foreign-Exchange Violation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends or partnering loans to foreign shareholders without applying the statutory 10% dividend WHT, or routing profit distributions through PayPal Mass Payout / Wise as alleged 'market research honoraria' absent an underlying commercial contract.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The remittance is recharacterised as a dividend subject to 10% WHT, plus a late-payment surcharge of 2% per month and an additional penalty of up to 100%; violation of Central Bank of Egypt foreign-exchange regulations can incur fines up to EGP 1,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorised the un-withheld distribution are jointly and severally liable for the withholding tax and surcharges; travel bans and asset seizure may be ordered for the recovery of public funds.
